newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sells Aerospostal for $20 mln.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sells Aerospostal for $20 mln.

text.p: After three failed attempts Venezuela successfully sold airline company Aeropostal for $20 million to the Venezuelan and U.S. consortium Corporacion Alas de Venezuela, the airline's receivers said.
The sale equalled the airline's base price. There were no other bidders.
"This is a great result... with this sale we've completed something that the whole country was waiting for," Servio Altuve, a member of the airline's board of creditors, told reporters.
Six groups of investors had originally shown interest in this latest bidding round.
But the U.K.'s World Aviation Group dropped out Tuesday critisizing the auction process as convoluted and unclear.
Three other groups never showed to bid at the Friday auction. And a fifth group, the U.S. owned James Bourke Air Fleet, failed to meet deposit requirements.
ALAS was formed last year by a group of Venezuelan and US investors. The airline will be its first operation.

Although the sale was executed by the airline's creditors, and not the government, it gives a welcome and needed boost to Venezuela's sagging privatization program.
Earlier this week, the government suspend the sales of Banco de Venezuela and aluminium concern Alucasa.
